findings.label: Paid During Active Breaches
findings.detail: 6 suppliers received payments while in breach of Companies Act — including 0 critical and 0 high severity. Temporally verified against payment dates.

findings.label: Suspected Split Payments
findings.detail: 173 instances of 3+ payments just below approval thresholds in the same week
findings.context_note: Split payment detection has a high false-positive rate. Batch processing, staged invoices, and legitimate recurring payments can all trigger this pattern. FOI request for procurement approval chain recommended before drawing conclusions.

findings.label: Round-Number Payments (>£5K)
findings.detail: 1373 exact round-number payments over £5,000 — may indicate estimates rather than invoiced amounts

findings.label: Rapid Payment Suppliers
findings.detail: 15 suppliers receive payments every <14 days on average. Top: Redacted - Payment To Individual (2.9 day avg, 13865 payments, £37.1M)

findings.label: Benford's Law Analysis
findings.detail: Digit distribution across 137,324 transactions shows χ²=5058.98 (statistically significant due to large sample size), but max digit deviation is only 3.8% — within the normal range for UK council spending patterns. No practical evidence of fabricated invoices.
findings.context_note: Chi-squared values on samples of 137,324+ transactions are naturally inflated and will almost always show statistical significance. The max digit deviation (3.8%) is a more meaningful indicator — deviations under 5% are typical for legitimate council spending.

findings.label: Second-Digit Benford's Anomaly
findings.detail: Second-digit distribution across 137,324 transactions shows p < 0.001 (highly significant). Digit 0 deviates 4.02% from Nigrini's expected distribution. Second-digit tests are more discriminating than first-digit for detecting round-number bias and fabricated invoices.
findings.context_note: Benford's second-digit analysis (Nigrini, 2012) uses chi-squared with 9 df. Critical values: 16.92 (p=0.05), 21.67 (p=0.01), 27.88 (p=0.001). n=137,324.

findings.label: Weak Competition Indicators
findings.detail: 65 contracts show signs of limited competition (short tender periods or rapid award). Top: GB-Durham: TPPL Durham County Council NEPO HGV lot (£3.7M)
findings.context_note: Contracts Finder does not publish bid counts. These flags use proxy signals: tender periods under 14 days and awards within 7 days of deadline. Short timelines may have legitimate explanations (framework call-offs, urgency).

findings.label: High-Risk Councillors
findings.detail: 21 councillors scored 'high risk' in integrity assessment across 36 data sources. Most common flags: undeclared interests, supplier conflicts, and company compliance issues.

key_findings.title: 6 suppliers with clock-like payment regularity
key_findings.description: These suppliers receive payments at near-identical intervals (std dev <5 days). Top: Reed Managed Services Ltd — every 3.2 days (39 payments, £85.5K)

key_findings.title: REDACTED - PAYMENT TO INDIVIDUAL: 13865 transactions totalling £37.1M
key_findings.description: Averaging £2.7K per transaction — the council's most frequent supplier

key_findings.title: 24 suppliers shared with neighbouring councils — £73.7M total
key_findings.description: Compare what each council pays the same suppliers for similar services

key_findings.title: HOLCIM UK LTD: 7074% price gap between councils
key_findings.description: Derbyshire_Cc pays £83.4K avg vs Doncaster £1.2K (both with 3+ transactions). Compared using 3 common financial years. Price differences may reflect different service scope, contract terms, or volumes rather than overcharging — manual review recommended.
key_findings.context_note: Cross-council price comparisons use common financial years only (where both councils have data for the same supplier). This prevents unfair comparisons between councils with different data periods. Differences may still reflect different service levels or contract terms.

key_findings.title: 1 service categories with a single supplier
key_findings.description: Top: Scarab Sweepers Limited — sole winner in 'Road sweepers' (2 contracts, £2.2M). Category monopolies may indicate market failure or specification bias.

key_findings.title: AI DOGE covers 28% of £1042.5M GOV.UK outturn
key_findings.description: Spending >£500 threshold means smaller transactions are excluded. Largest gaps: Education services, Highways and transport services, Children Social Care. This is expected — not a data quality issue.
